legend: Panoramic view showing the border between tumour and normal cardiac myocytes.
At high magnification, enlarged swollen myocytes with clear cytoplasm are visible. Strands of cytoplasm are connected to the peripheral cell membrane.
The swollen cardiac myocytes are full of glycogen, shown on PAS stain.
Autopsy specimen demonstrating multiple cardiac rhabdomyomas involving the left ventricle. The masses can be seen obstructing the ventricular outflow tract.
2D echocardiography showing an intracavitary rhabdomyoma of the right ventricular outflow tract.

diagnosis: Cardiac rhabdomyoma of the left ventricle
legend: Electrocardiography-triggered breath-hold proton density T1-weighted fast spin-echo in coronal plane, showing a large homogeneous isointense mass involving the left ventricular wall. Ao, aorta; RA, right atrium.

legend: A collection of large vacuolated myocytes forms an intramyocardial tumour. Classic "spider cells," that have radial sarcoplasmic strands that extend from the centrally placed nuclei to the sarcoplasmic membrane, can be seen.
